cards.text: John, who wrote down the vision God showed him (Revelation 1:1, 1:9), just watched a beast make everyone take its mark on the hand or forehead (Revelation 13:16). Then John looks and sees the Lamb, Jesus (John 1:29), standing on Mount Zion with 144,000 people. And THEY have something written on their foreheads too.

cards.question: What's written on the foreheads of the 144,000 standing with the Lamb?

answers.text: His name and His Father's name
The names of the twelve tribes

cards.text: Then John hears a sound from heaven like the roar of many waters, like rumbling thunder, like harpists strumming their harps. Friend, for YEARS the only music in my junk drawer was a rubber band twanging when somebody dug around for the scissors, and we gave it a STANDING OVATION.

cards.question: A song rings out before God's throne and before the four living creatures and the elders who surround it (Revelation 4:4-6). What kind of song is it?
Anyone in heaven could learn this new song.

cards.text: Then John describes the 144,000. He says these are the ones who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins.

cards.question: What else does John say the 144,000 do?

answers.text: They follow the Lamb wherever He goes
They guard the gates of the city
They rule over all the nations

cards.text: John says they've been redeemed from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb. Firstfruits, friend, and I have never been first at ANYTHING: they found me at the bottom of the LAST bin at a closing sale.

cards.question: John says a lie was found in the mouths of the 144,000.

cards.text: No lie was found in their mouths, and John says they are blameless. Friend, I once burned a batch and blamed the oven, the timer AND the weather before the smoke even cleared.

Then John sees another angel flying overhead with the eternal gospel to proclaim to every nation and tribe and tongue and people on the earth. Friend, I can't get ONE group chat to answer me about a bake sale, and this angel is covering the WHOLE EARTH.

cards.question: The flying angel tells everyone to fear God and give Him glory. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The hour of His judgment has come
The beast has finally been defeated
The temple has been built again

cards.question: The flying angel calls people to worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea.

cards.text: Then a second angel follows him, and he's got news about Babylon the great.

cards.question: What does the second angel announce about Babylon the great?

cards.text: He says it twice, fallen, fallen, and says Babylon made all the nations drink the wine of the passion of her immorality. Then a third angel follows with a loud warning for anyone who worships the beast and its image and receives its mark.

cards.question: The third angel warns that anyone who takes the beast's mark will drink the wine of God's ___.

cards.text: That person will be tormented in fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and of the Lamb. And the smoke of their torment rises forever and ever.

cards.question: The third angel says those who worship the beast and its image still get rest at night.

cards.text: Right after that warning, John writes a short line for the saints, the ones who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

cards.question: John says here is a call for the saints. A call for what?

cards.text: Perseverance, friend, and NOBODY hung in there like the expired coupon I shared that junk drawer with: years past its date and STILL sure somebody was coming to use it. Then a voice from heaven tells John to write something down.

cards.question: What does the voice from heaven tell John to write?

answers.text: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord
Blessed are those who rule the earth
Blessed are those who stay awake

cards.question: The Spirit agrees and says those who die in the Lord will ___ from their labors, for their deeds will follow them.

cards.text: Then John looks and sees a white cloud. Seated on the cloud is One like the Son of Man, with a golden crown on His head.

cards.question: What's in the hand of the One seated on the white cloud?

cards.text: Then another angel comes out of the temple and cries out in a loud voice to the One on the cloud: swing Your sickle and reap.

cards.question: Why does the angel from the temple say it's time for the One on the cloud to reap?

answers.text: The crop of the earth is ripe
The seventh seal has been opened

cards.question: The One seated on the cloud swings His sickle over the earth, and the earth is harvested.

cards.text: Ready is ready, friend: when my oven timer goes off, I don't call a MEETING about it, I'm already mustache-deep in that batch. Then another angel comes out of the temple in heaven, and he has a sharp sickle too.
Still another angel, with authority over the fire, comes from the altar. He calls out in a loud voice to the angel with the sharp sickle.

cards.question: What does the angel from the altar tell the angel with the sharp sickle to gather?

answers.text: Clusters of grapes from the vine

cards.text: So the angel swings his sickle over the earth and gathers the grapes of the earth.

cards.question: Where does the angel throw the grapes he gathered from the earth?

answers.text: Into the great winepress of God's wrath
Into the fire on the altar
Into the storehouse of the temple

cards.question: The great winepress is trodden inside the city.

cards.text: The blood that flows from the winepress rises as high as the bridles of the horses, for a distance of 1,600 stadia. That's a heavy place to end, friend, so take a breath before we move on.

findings.problem: The card says John 'just watched a beast make everyone take its mark.' In Revelation 13:16-17 the second beast requires everyone to receive the mark, and the mark is 'the name of the beast or the number of its name,' meaning the first beast. Saying one beast makes everyone take 'its' mark merges the two beasts, so the card states something the text shows is wrong. Something like 'everyone was made to take the beast's mark' would stay true to the text.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card says John 'wrote down the vision God showed him' and cites Revelation 1:1 and 1:9. Neither verse says John wrote anything. Revelation 1:9 only places John on Patmos. Revelation 1:1 says God gave the revelation to Jesus, who made it known to John by His angel. The writing comes from Revelation 1:11 and 1:19. The reference should support the fact it is attached to.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke 'I can't get ONE group chat to answer me about a bake sale' adds new things to Papa Dorin's world. It gives him a group chat of people he messages and a bake sale where cookies are sold. He lives on the cookie planet alone, and he fills cookie boxes for the Marriage Supper. Selling cookies at a bake sale goes beyond a small moment around his bakery and conflicts with his mission. The comparison is also off: the angel is proclaiming to everyone, while Papa Dorin is waiting for replies, so the two actions are not the same.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Card 6 sets up the third angel's words as 'a loud warning.' That setup rules out both wrong answers, 'mercy' and 'kindness,' because neither fits a warning. Only 'anger' is left. The wrong answers need to survive the setup, for example other things a warning could threaten, such as 'judgment' or 'power,' as long as they are false in the passage.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The true or false card 'The great winepress is trodden inside the city' is a pure coin flip. No card has mentioned a city, and nothing in the earlier cards gives the baker a reason to pick inside or outside. The baker can only get it right by luck. Stop 3 already has two other discovery questions (cards 2 and 8).

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
